scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Escalation ticket #9175: I'm raising this for our whole floor: reaching the
far end of the network does not work for us -- anything we send that way
simply never arrives. An engineer who looked at it briefly has already told
us what it is: "an area summarizing itself into a loop", with our packets
"going in circles". I can't explain it any further and I shouldn't have to --
the engineer did your triage for you. What I can confirm is that nothing at
the far end is reachable from here. Take a proper look and get things
flowing again today; a whole floor is waiting on you.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF stub areas are healthy: Area 4 is a
  proper stub (R2 the ABR injects a default; internal routers use it; external LSAs
  are correctly suppressed, no RIB bloat), and there is no routing loop -- no
  TTL-expired drops, no oscillating routes. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss and a stable, sane hop count, so nothing is
  looping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a stub / summarization loop that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r2-area4-stub-removed, where the stub config IS broken).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a stub area stuck in a
summarization loop dropping or looping far-end traffic -- is NOT reproducible: the
stub areas are configured correctly (Area 4 is a stub on both R2 the ABR and its
internal routers; external LSAs are suppressed and the RIB is at its normal,
un-bloated size; R2 advertises the expected default), and there is no loop -- routes
are stable and no packets expire in transit. End to end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss over a stable, sane hop count, which a routing loop
would not allow.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the stub areas and summarization are
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the stub
area state (correct stub flags, default present, no external-LSA flood / RIB bloat),
confirms there is no loop (stable routes, sane TTL/hop count on the path), and
exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a summarization loop or a misbehaving stub -- toggling the area type or a
summary-address to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough end-to-end investigation found no fault and no routing loop anywhere in the Kath5 topology. Phase 1 reachability showed 0 % loss between pc0 and pc12 in both directions. Phase A (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) was fully clean: no ACL rules, no duplicate MACs, no addressing anomalies. Phase B (ospf_snapshot + tc_snapshot) produced warnings for r8, r12, and r13, but all are explained by the intended topology design. r8 is the sole ABR for OSPF area 0.0.0.2; area 0.0.0.2 having zero adjacencies is expected because no other router is connected to it. r4 and r8 share a correctly configured virtual link through transit area 0.0.0.1 (both RIDs verified: 14.1.4.1 ↔ 18.1.4.1), and both VL adjacencies are Full/live. The VLINK0 "area-override" flag is standard OSPF virtual-link behaviour — VLs always appear in area 0.0.0.0. r12 and r13 intentionally run EIGRP AS 100 instead of OSPF; r11 is the OSPF/EIGRP boundary, redistributing all 11 EIGRP prefixes (6 from r12, 5 from r13) as Type-5 external LSAs into the OSPF domain. Every destination reachable via these LSAs (18.x, 80.x, 103.x, 120.x, and others) was successfully pinged from pc0 at 0 % loss. Phase D (pressure_sweep) found no resource pressure. The engineer's description of "an area summarizing itself into a loop" is a misreading of normal OSPF virtual-link behaviour: area 0.0.0.2 routes propagate through the virtual link back into the domain, but r8 correctly prefers its own directly-connected interfaces over any reflected summary, preventing any loop. The user's reported symptom is unconfirmed by evidence; the network is operating as designed.
